knowledge_graph.title: Disease model of addiction
knowledge_graph.description: The disease model of addiction describes an addiction as a disease with genetic, biological, neurological or environmental origin. The traditional medical model of disease requires only an abnormal condition causing distress, discomfort or dysfunction to an affected individual.

text_blocks.snippet: The "disease model of addiction" posits that addiction is a chronic, relapsing brain disease characterized by compulsive substance use despite harmful consequences. It views addiction not as a moral failing or a matter of willpower, but as a medical condition influenced by a combination of genetic, biological, environmental, and psychological factors. This model emphasizes that addiction involves changes in brain structure and function, particularly in the reward, motivation, and self-control pathways, leading to persistent changes in behavior.
